plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Static gain magnitude and dominant lag/settling time, which set the feedforward to hold 0.5 and safe feedback aggressiveness; currently completely unmeasured.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises monotonically from ~0.05 after a short lag, reaching roughly 0.2-0.4 by 180 s with still-positive end slope, confirming positive gain and substantial lag without reaching equilibrium.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Settling time and equilibrium gain at u=0.5 and whether its steady state lies above target 0.5, which sets feedforward for 0.5 and safe feedback aggressiveness.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises monotonically from ~0.395 to ~0.53-0.58 with still-positive but declining end slope ~0.0008-0.0013, confirming equilibrium for u=0.5 is above 0.5 and time constant is several hundred seconds, without approaching soft limit.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Self-cooling decay rate and falling time constant at u=0 (H4), currently inferred only, which sets heat-loss, settling time, and safe integral/feedback aggressiveness for control.
experiments.expected_observation: y decays monotonically from ~0.486 toward ~0.20-0.25 over 180 s with negative slope that flattens in magnitude but remains negative at end, confirming self-cooling heat loss and falling time constant ~150-200 s symmetrical to heating.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain linearity and u needed to hold y=0.5 (H5/H7), which sets feedforward and steady-state error; single level u=0.5 cannot separate linear gain from saturation.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises monotonically from ~0.19 to ~0.39-0.42 over 180 s with still-positive but declining end slope ~0.0005-0.0009, confirming equilibrium near 0.51 for u=0.45 and linear gain ~1.0 without approaching soft limit.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state feedforward to hold y=0.5 and linearity near target, which sets tracking error and energy; inferred only from extrapolation of unsettled responses at 0.5 and 0.45.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises slowly from ~0.40 to ~0.45-0.47 over 180 s with small declining but still-positive end slope ~0.0003-0.0006, confirming equilibrium near 0.50 for u~0.41 and linear gain ~1.1 without approaching soft limit.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state feedforward to hold y=0.5 and linearity near target, which sets tracking error and energy; currently interpolated from unsettled 0.5 and 0.45 and E5 at 0.41, not directly observed at target.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises slowly from ~0.448 to ~0.47-0.48 over 140 s with small declining but still-positive end slope ~0.0001-0.0003, confirming equilibrium near 0.49-0.51 for u=0.44 and that u~0.44 holds target.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state feedforward to hold y=0.5 and linearity near target, which sets tracking error and energy; E5-E6 suggest 0.44 is slightly low but have not observed convergence to 0.5 from inside the band.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises slowly from ~0.475 to ~0.495-0.505 over 120 s with declining but still slightly positive end slope, confirming y_ss for 0.47 is ~0.52 and that u~0.45-0.46 holds y=0.5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state feedforward to hold y=0.5 and linearity near target, which sets tracking error and energy; extrapolated only from unsettled rises, not yet observed as a flat hold in the band.
experiments.expected_observation: y holds near 0.50, drifting only slightly from 0.502 to ~0.498-0.508 over 120 s with near-zero end slope, confirming y_ss for u=0.45 is ~0.50 and u~0.45-0.46 holds target.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Pure delay and passive cooling rate at u=0, which discriminates faster outflow (faster fall) from weaker actuator (same fall as E3) and slower response (longer wait before fall) and reveals sensor offset; required to reset feedforward and safe feedback aggressiveness.
experiments.expected_observation: If slower response is right, y stays flat or keeps responding to prior ~0.67 command for 20-60 s after switch to 0, then falls slowly; if faster outflow, fall starts in ~6-12 s and is steeper than E3; if weaker actuator only, delay ~6-12 s and fall matches E3; sensor offset would show as constant bias versus E3 trajectory.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Heating static gain magnitude and new feedforward u to hold 0.5, which discriminates weaker actuator from faster outflow when combined with identical E9 cooling and sets safe feedback aggressiveness.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker actuator is right, y holds near 0.11 for ~6-12 s then rises monotonically with same 0.0054 quantization but ~25-35% smaller slope than E1, reaching ~0.27-0.32 by 200 s with still-positive end slope, versus 0.395 in E1; faster outflow would have shown faster E9 fall which it did not, longer delay would have shown continued rise after switch which E9 did not, sensor offset would show as bias versus E3 trajectory.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: New heating static gain magnitude and feedforward u to hold 0.5 and linearity near target, which sets tracking error and safe aggressiveness; E10 shows weaker rise but is far from equilibrium and alone cannot separate gain factor from required u_hold.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker actuator is right, y rises after ~6-12 s from ~0.309 to ~0.39-0.42 over 120 s with still-positive end slope ~0.0004-0.0008 and same 0.0054 quantization, implying y_ss for 0.7 ~0.43-0.47 and u~0.8-0.85 needed for 0.5; faster outflow would have shown faster E9 fall which it did not, longer delay would show >20 s flat after switch which it will not, sensor offset/gain would show bias vs E3/E1 trajectories.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: New heating static gain factor and feedforward u to hold 0.5 near target, which sets tracking error and energy; E10-E11 are far below target and only extrapolate u_hold ~0.66.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker-actuator is right, y stays ~0.427 for 6-12 s then rises monotonically with same 0.0054 quantization to ~0.47-0.48 over 100 s with still-positive end slope ~0.0003-0.0006, implying y_ss for 0.65 ~0.49-0.51 and u_hold ~0.65-0.68; longer delay would stay flat >20 s, faster outflow would already have shown faster E9 fall which it did not, sensor offset would show as bias vs E1/E3.

ledger.statement: Increasing steady heater power u increases steady temperature y (positive static gain).
Step response is lagged, not instantaneous: pure delay only ~6-12 s but first-order settling takes >500 s total, time constant ~150-170 s.
No large dead zone: u at or above 0.41 produces a clear positive slope, i.e. dead zone if any is below 0.4.
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.05 (self-cooling heat loss).
Pre-change steady-state y is approximately linear in u with gain ~1.0 above ambient ~0.05, so the u needed to hold y=0.5 was in mid-range 0.4-0.5.
Sensor short-term noise and fluctuations are small, less than 0.01 peak-to-peak with ~0.005 quantization, relative to the 0.05 target band.
Pre-change equilibrium y for u=0.5 is ~0.55, for u=0.47 is ~0.52, for u=0.45 is ~0.50, for u=0.44 is ~0.49 and for u=0.41 is ~0.46, so holding y=0.5 required u ~0.45-0.46.
Change is weaker actuator: same u gives ~30-35% smaller steady rise (factor ~0.65-0.70), ~50% smaller initial rise slope, but u=0 cooling rate and pure delay are unchanged from H2/H4.
Change is faster outflow/heat loss: u=0 fall is faster than E3 and same u holds lower steady y, requiring higher u to hold 0.5.
Change is slower response: pure delay from COMMAND LAST CHANGED to first visible move is much longer than 6-12 s and/or approach is slower, with steady gain similar.
Change is sensor change: measurement offset, gain, quantization or noise changed while true thermal response is unchanged.
